Clothing & Textile Restoration

Fire, Smoke & Soot Damage Clothing Restoration in Pennsylvania

After a fire, clothing and household textiles can be affected by soot, airborne smoke residue, odor, heat and firefighting water. The visible damage does not always tell the full story.

What happens to clothing after a fire?

Soot and smoke residue can settle into fabric, linings, seams, folds and stored garments. Heat may also change the strength, finish or color of some materials. Different textiles react differently, so the first question is what has happened to each item—not how quickly it can be washed.

What items may be considered?

Everyday clothing, business attire, uniforms, bedding, linens, drapery and certain specialty garments may be assessed for restoration. Condition, material and extent of exposure affect the outcome. Some items may not be suitable for restoration.

Before you handle affected textiles

Avoid rubbing soot into fabric or attempting aggressive home cleaning. Keep unaffected items separate from affected items where practical. For heavily contaminated items or potentially hazardous residue, wait for appropriate clearance and professional guidance.

What to expect from an assessment

When you contact American Clothing Restoration, describe the source of damage, the types of garments involved, and any known exposure to heat, soot, smoke or water. ACR can discuss the next step; restoration and results depend on the actual condition of the items.

The next step

Ask about your affected clothing and textiles.
